summary: Docs-only commit: ADR-0036 plus SPEC.md criteria 6/9 and two test-matrix rows. No test files staged, so the review is of whether the criteria and matrix rows, as written, would fail against a wrong implementation. Round-13 minor 3 is closed and its mutation is dead: `commitAll`'s distinct-key rule is on segmentKey only (CommitLog.java:292-300), so one pod at flushSeq 0 and 1 in ONE batch is legal, which makes 'a replay the pointed delta DOES carry' constructible below the watermark and kills `if (flushSeq < lastApplied) return REFUSE;` ahead of the read. F1 is fixed: the criteria list now numbers 1..12 with no duplicate, so check-milestone-verified.sh cannot discharge two obligations with one line. F2's premise is verified true in the tree (LocalSequencer.java:349-353 calls observe only after commitAll returns), and criterion 6 now states it correctly. Every claim ADR-0036 makes about an existing test was checked and is true (BatchedCommitDeltaTest three-segment/three-pod round-trip with per-segment assertions; BatchingSequencerTest:93,261 hasSize(2) with flushSeq 0 for every pod; CheckpointTest:153-169 <64 KiB at 1,600 streams; CheckpointDecodeRefusalTest:117 bytes[7]=1 against Checkpoint.VERSION=0's strict equality; golden/chain-delta-batched-v1.bin holds bins/a.seg and bins/b.seg with no pod in either key). CheckpointWriter.java:105-106 is in the sites list (backlog-notes.md:312). No existing assertion was weakened -- no test file is staged. Three minors, all remediable by one clause each.

findings.title: The new T1 GET row says 'every replay answered' but never says answered WITH WHAT, so answering all six from the shared delta's first entry is green
findings.failure_scenario: The row's fixture -- 6 replaying pods whose pointers name ONE delta -- is the only place in the matrix where a shared delta is read on behalf of several pods, and it is exactly where picking the wrong entry out of that delta is the likely bug. The row constrains the GET COUNT (exactly one) and the ANSWER COUNT (every replay answered) and nothing about the answer's content. So a dedup that GETs the pointed delta once and returns its FIRST SegmentCommit's RunCommit.firstOffset to all six replayers issues exactly one GET, answers every replay, and is green -- while five of six producers are handed another flush's offsets. ADR-0036 names this hazard in its own words ('Returning the pointed delta's offsets would hand back another flush's firstOffset -- the invariant M4.46 names'), and criterion 6's 'returns the original assignment' is the clause that forbids it, but criterion 6 carries no multi-pod shared-delta fixture; this row is the one that does. Remedy: 'and every replay answered WITH ITS OWN original offsets', and put 'a lookup that answers every replayer from the pointed delta's first entry' in the mutation column beside the two already there.
findings.surviving_mutation: In the answering path, replace the lookup of the exact (podId, incarnationId, flushSeq) inside the pointed delta with `delta.allRuns().get(0).firstOffset()` for every replayer -- one GET, six answers, row green.

findings.location: docs/internal/product/milestones/M4/SPEC.md:423-429 (criterion 6) vs the test matrix at :493 and :496
findings.title: Criterion 6's ambiguous-commit clause -- the F2 fix -- has no row in the test matrix, and the matrix's own rows are all satisfied by an in-memory-only dedup
findings.failure_scenario: Criterion 6 now correctly says the pointer is recorded only for commits the leader OBSERVES applying, that an ambiguous commit is not one, and that M4.10d must reconcile it from the chain. That obligation exists in criterion prose only. Both idempotency rows in the matrix -- the T0 row at :493 and the new T1 row at :496 -- have fixtures in which commitAll RETURNS, so LocalSequencer.java:353 runs observe and the in-memory window learns the triple. An implementation whose dedup consults only CheckpointWriter's pods map and the recovered window, and never reads the chain, is therefore green on the entire matrix while double-assigning offsets for exactly the ambiguous PUT the milestone exists to make safe. The spec's own preamble at :480-481 says the mutation column is what makes each row worth having, and the mutation with the largest blast radius has no column to sit in. It is buildable today, not blocked on M4.12: FaultInjectingStore's ambiguous-putIfAbsent arm already exists (FaultInjectingStoreTest.java:279-289), and the M4.10d notes already call it 'the existing seam'. Remedy: one row -- 'T1 | Replay after an AMBIGUOUS commit (the PUT landed, commitAll threw, observe never ran) is detected and answered from the CHAIN | a dedup that consults only the in-memory window -- green against every successful-commit fixture'.
findings.surviving_mutation: Delete the chain read from the dedup path entirely and key it on the in-memory pods map alone: both matrix rows stay green, and the ambiguous-commit replay is assigned a second offset range.

findings.title: Folding the GET clause into criterion 9 left a truncated duplicate sentence, so the GET obligation is wedged inside a sentence that stops mid-clause
findings.failure_scenario: Line 456 reads '⚠️ The saturation clause matters: "unchanged" alone is' and ends there; the folded GET paragraph follows at 457-461; the same sentence starts again, complete this time, at 462-464. The fold was made precisely so that one criterion-9 evidence line in VERIFIED.md cannot discharge the PUT half while leaving the GET half unproven, but check-milestone-verified.sh only requires the line to name a test -- so the reader's understanding of what criterion 9 demands is the whole defence, and that reader now hits a sentence that breaks off immediately before the GET clause, making the GET clause read as an interpolation rather than as a clause of the criterion. Remedy: delete line 456; the sentence is already intact at 462.
findings.surviving_mutation: n/a -- corrupted acceptance-criterion text in the staged bytes rather than a code mutation; the concrete consequence is stated above.
